swing_ideas.text: Cup and handle forming a long term rounded base. If price can remain over 41.7 and breakout over 48.4, looking for action to attempt a gap close.
Inverted head and shoulders setting up a trend line break as the neckline. Gap overhead becomes the target. In play as long as price remains over 22.75 neckline area.

Very strong uptrend on the daily and even weekly timeframe charts. Great set of higher lows and higher highs. Looking for a break of the resistance trend line if we can continue holding over 174.85 - 171.8 zone. Prior resistance acting as new support. Under that zone and its out of play.

Massive retest of the breakout level. If the 35 level breaks, could classify as a double bottom reversal off of prior resistance now acting as support. First target is the double top neckline at 36.75 and then beyond that we have the highs at 39.15 area. Out of play if price breaks and closes below 33.70 area.

The cyber theme should be in play through 2025 as AI scales and geopolitical tensions remain... elevated let's say. Looking to see if this penant can take out 99.65 and move into blue sky territory. Any higher lows ideally hold the support trend line.

Another retest setup where prior resistance can act as support. Liking the hammer from the Friday session indicating sellers were unable to materialize on the Thursday momentum even after breaking the low. Ideally there is a full rotation up towards 63.3, but mind the lower high in there around 61.

sections: S&P monthly chart – December pulled back, but only about to the mid point of the November range. December also made a new ATH. Overall trend is up and will remain up on any higher low over ~530.

S&P weekly chart – Green bodied hammer closed, the exact opposite of the week prior. Still wicking off of 585, the key level to sustain the weekly higher low. Still holding: fib 61.8, weekly breakout aVWAP, HVN.

S&P daily chart – The dreaded head & shoulders everyone is concerned about in cyan... More appropriately, early week focus should be on the 595.25 and 590.75 levels. Those hold the key to bull or bear. In between, I expect balance. With labor data this week... not likely to stay between.

S&P hourly chart – Most important point here is the failure of sellers to materialize on the move lower from Thursday. No lower high under range, no rejection of the top of range. This gives buyers an edge into the early week.

Market internals – Focus on the Thursday session. The day where markets arguably had the most bearish intraday price movement. Internals surprisingly were NOT bearish. Definitely not a raging bullish session, but this is not what new money selling looks like.

Market profile – Value shifted higher on Friday which supports buyers having that subtle edge. If money was flowing into the market on Thursday (internals suggest yes), then buyers have great location.
